M-E-002.mitigation: Implement proper ACLs and role-based access control

M-E-007.mitigation: Implement application whitelisting — only explicitly authorized binaries may execute

M-E-008.mitigation: Deploy antivirus / EDR software and keep signatures up to date

M-NET-001.mitigation: Configure an inbound firewall with default deny — only explicitly needed ports and peers are reachable

M-NET-003.mitigation: Disable unused ports, services and protocols — keep a minimal attack surface per build

M-NET-004.mitigation: Bind services to internal interfaces only — no management or debug service on external interfaces

M-AC-001.mitigation: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) with defined roles and least-privileged role assignment

M-AC-002.mitigation: Implement attribute-based access control (ABAC) — decisions use attributes such as operating state, location, time or vehicle speed

M-AC-003.mitigation: Run each service under its own unprivileged account — no root, unneeded capabilities dropped

M-OS-001.mitigation: Enforce mandatory access control (SELinux or AppArmor) in enforcing mode with a profile per service

M-OS-002.mitigation: Restrict system calls of exposed services with seccomp filters

M-OS-004.mitigation: Harden the kernel — no unused modules, lockdown mode, hardened sysctl settings

M-OS-006.mitigation: Apply a hardening baseline (e.g. CIS benchmark) and check it automatically for every release

M-OPS-001.mitigation: Monitor vulnerabilities and manage patches for all third-party and OS components, based on an SBOM
